ingredients.cook_qty: 1 tsp on the jicama plus 2 tsp for the side

instructions: Peel the jicama with a vegetable peeler. Cut it into sticks about 1/2 inch thick and 3 inches long and transfer them to a bowl.
Squeeze the juice of the lime over the sticks. Sprinkle on 1 tsp of the chili powder and the salt and toss until every stick is coated.
Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro and toss it through.
Put the remaining 2 tsp chili powder in a small bowl for anyone who wants more heat. Serve the sticks with the bowl of chili powder on the side.
method_notes: No version has a rating, so this is a fallback. FoodShare South Carolina leads: jicama sticks with lime juice, chili powder, salt and chopped cilantro, with nothing cooked. Food.com serves the jicama with lime wedges and a chili salt to dip, and The Splendid Table adds mango and uses about 1 tsp of chile for a pound of jicama. The lead's 1 tbsp of chili powder is kept, but only 1 tsp goes on the sticks and the rest is served on the side to keep the base mild. Check the chili powder label if gluten matters.
